successors.name: Bali (the Nine Kingdoms)
successors.text: Bali island, the Nine Kingdoms period with its seat at Klungkung

ledger.x: 1478: the Gelgel kingdom of Bali begins after Majapahit's vassalage.

c. 1519: Blambangan under Gelgel's suzerainty. 'Gelgel reached its apogee during the reign of Dalem Baturenggong, as Lombok, western Sumbawa and Blambangan on easternmost Java, were united under Gelgel's suzerainty.' The page dates the reign c. 1460-1550 or the 'mid-16th century' (text) and no conquest; 1519…

c. 1519: eastern Lombok and western Sumbawa under Gelgel's suzerainty (same sentence, same undated apogee). The Lombok page disagrees: before the 17th century Lombok was 'numerous competing and feuding petty states' under Sasak princes.
c. 1609: the Balinese take western Lombok. 'the neighbouring Balinese who took control of western Lombok in the early seventeenth century'.
1618: Makassar attacks Sumbawa and, from there, eastern Lombok.

c. 1683: Lombok leaves the Gelgel shape as the kingdom breaks up. 'After 1651 the Gelgel kingdom began to break up due to internal conflicts.' The year is Cliopatria's; no page dates the loss, and the Lombok page has the Balinese on western Lombok through the century.
1686: a new royal seat at Klungkung.
1686: the Gelgel kingdom ends and the Nine Kingdoms period begins.

wars.name: Balinese attack on Blambangan
wars.outcome: No territorial result recorded: 'Blambangan was attacked by Balinese kingdom: 1501' (Blambangan page).

wars.name: Makassar's attacks on Sumbawa and Lombok
wars.outcome: The Gowa page dates the first Makassar attack on Sumbawa to 1618; the Lombok page has the Makassarese invading eastern Lombok from Sumbawa while the Balinese held the west.

wars.name: Mataram's invasion of Blambangan
wars.outcome: 'In 1639 Mataram launched an invasion to Blambangan'; Blambangan surrendered but 'quickly regained their independence', with Gelgel supporting it as a buffer.

certainty.note: Bali's coastline gives the island a sharp edge; the suzerainty over Lombok, Sumbawa and Blambangan has no border at all and is soft.
